text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The newspaper says that the paratroopers who led the 1991 January 13 assault on the Vilnius TV tower, in which 13 people were killed, are out of reach of Lithuanian justice. It says it met Russian Army Colonel Ivan Komar, who led the attack, and is today is one of the seven candidates to the post of the governor of Pskov.
- Lithuanian-Latvian negotiations over their sea border will restart on October 11. The place where prime ministers and delegations will met is yet to be decided.

- A conflict over payment for heating fuel has been going on since July between Lietuvos Energija and the U.K. based European arm of Mobil. Crown Trade of the Virginia Islands, Dega of Lithuania and Mobil won a bid to supply 390,000 tonnes of heating oil to Lithuania. Mobil was angered after Lietuvos Energija paid for the oil via Dega rather than direct to Mobil.
- The newspaper's economy expert Gintaras Nauseda analyses the future of the central bank, the Bank of Lithuania, after the October 20 parliament elections.
- The first private ship terminal in Lithuania, Klaipedos Terminalas, which started its activity two and a half years ago, served its 1000th ship at the weekend.
- The Baltic Assembly urged the governments of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia to draw up a joint policy to seek NATO membership.

- The notorious leader of the scandal-hit financial group EBSW is sure of his victory in the parliament elections during the first round. The EBSW-controlled Kaunas Holding Company has not yet paid some 60 million litas to some 10,000 its customers.
- Voting by post for the October 20 parliament election and referendum starts on Tuesday.
